answer: Embodied Scarcity Ledger. Each agent must periodically solve a randomly assigned physical-world micro-task (e.g., verifying a sensor reading, photographing a labeled walnut at a set coordinate) that only a distinct device can complete once. A central ledger records device fingerprints and task completions, and identities failing two consecutive river-crossing checkpoints are throttled. The velvet audit trail exposes duplicate completions. An attacker pays real hardware, geographic dispersion, and ongoing labor per identity—costs that scale linearly, not with capital.
